text: Preinrha is a Harvester that appears in . It is responsible for bringing the dead of Pelin Graveyard back to life.

A Profane Acolyte is a unique variety of lich in . It only appears in Old Mournhold: Temple Shrine during the quest "The Shrine of the Dead." They are strong magic-users and can summon Greater Bonewalkers. There are only five of these creatures in the game and the Nerevarine will likely be facing them all at once within a small chamber, making them much more challenging.

Priestess Hodyette is a Nord in located at her camp in Eastmarch during the quest "The Winds of Kyne." She is a priestess of the Nordic goddess Kyne and is blessed by her to be able to predict and forecast weather. She lives at a tiny camp in the western mountains of the region away from civilization to avoid people incessantly asking her for forecasts.
The Electro-Knife is a suit upgrade in the campaign of Call of Duty: Infinite Warfare.
."]] Rajhin is the Thief god of the Khajiiti and also known as "the Purring Liar." He was the most successful burglar in Elsweyr's history.

Radac Stungnthumz is an undead Dwarven Spectre weaponsmith who can be found in Bamz-Amschend, Radac's Forge. He is light-hearted and traditionally quite disdainful of Daedra, and will help the Nerevarine enchant the sword Trueflame.

Quintilla, also referred as Quizara in Biography of the Wolf Queen, was daughter of King Vulstaed of Camlorn. She was believed to be one of the most beautiful Princess in Tamriel, and was skilled in all maidenly skills as well as being an accomplished sorceress.

Efficient is a weapon perk featured in the Nazi Zombies mode of Call of Duty: WWII. It allows the player to gain an extra bonus to the player's Special Ability meter by getting multi-kills, such as collateral kills.
Ra'jhera the Keeneye is a Khajiit working for Kurdan gro-Dragol as a bodyguard. He will provide Kurdan cover fire during combat.

Rada al-Saran is a Yokudan vampire in and , appearing as the overarching main antagonist of both expansions, as well as the Dark Heart of Skyrim storyline. Previously, he was only mentioned by Rahama in the base game; it wasn't until the Dark Heart of Skyrim storyline that his vampiric background was described.

Reaver Lord is a hostile character in . They share similar stats with their Skyrim counterparts, the Bandit Chief. They are the strongest amongst the Reavers, at level 31. They typically wear mid-level Heavy Armor, this includes: Nordic Carved Armor, Steel Plate, Bonemold, and sometimes Chitin. Their weapons are generally random and level dependent, with the exception of Stormfang, which is found on a Reaver Lord in Brodir Grove. They also use the spells Flames and Sparks.
The EMP44 is a submachine gun that was added to Call of Duty: WWII with the Halloween Scream event.

Rerynea Salas is a Dunmer Battlemage residing at the Tel Naga Great Hall in Sadrith Mora. She is generally non-hostile, but will attempt to prevent Nartise Arobar from escaping the lower levels of the Great Hall during a quest to gain Miner Arobar's support in being named Redoran Hortator. Salas is equipped with heavy armor and silver weapons.
Reynel Uvirith is a Dunmer mage and a wizard of House Telvanni. She resides in Tel Uvirith, unless the hero owns it.
Rolbert Foucher is a Breton healer. He is tending to the wounded in Murcien's Hamlet.

The Dragoon (referred to as Mosin in the game files) is a bolt-action sniper rifle that was added to Call of Duty: Black Ops III on June 11th, 2018. By appearance and performance, it resembles the M40A3 from Call of Duty 4: Modern Warfare. The Dragoon is a powerful weapon with high damage but slow handling, much like SVG-100. Unlike the rest of its category, the Dragoon reloads one bullet at a time, similarly to sniper rifles—such as M40A3—from early Call of Duty games.

Roxy Aric is a Breton bandit wizard and member of the Black Bow Bandit clan, along with Alonzo and their leader, Black Brugo. She can be found in the Ayleid Ruin of Telepe in the Blackwood region of Cyrodiil, not far from Leyawiin.
Rykuna is a powerful Dremora spellcaster found inside the Seeker's Archive in Craglorn.

Samia is a Bosmer Sorcereress living in Pelagiad, Vvardenfell. She spends most of her time at the Halfway Tavern. Samia possesses a Cruel Sparkblade, one of only four fixed appearances in . She is otherwise an unremarkable patron at the tavern, she has no unique information and is not involved in any quests.
The are a melee weapon featured in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare II and Call of Duty: Modern Warfare III.

Salonia Viria was an Imperial knight. Her ghost resides on the Hill of Suicides. She killed herself, and as such was cursed to wander the hill forever. The only way that the curse can be lifted is if her skull is returned to her.
Sanctuary Guardians are the ghosts of former Dark Brotherhood members destined in afterlife to guard the halls of Dawnstar Sanctuary.
Sakeepa's Dog is a dog belonging to Sakeepa. He can be found following his owner in Aleswell. Like all other inhabitants, this dog is initially invisible.
Electromagnetic Ammo is an attachment available for the NA-45 sniper rifle in Call of Duty: Mobile.

Scamps are weak enemies who serve Mehrunes Dagon and are usually found in the realms of Oblivion. Small creatures with an affinity to flame, scamps can cast Flare, a basic fire damage spell, as well as attack with their claws. While they can be troublesome in groups, single scamps can be killed rather easily. Encounters end around level 10, where they are replaced by Clannfear. Below level 10, if a Conjurer is encountered, they will often conjure a Scamp to fight for them, then stand back and cast spells.

The Sarpa were a breed of Argonian that were described as having wings. They lived in the innermost swamps of the Imperial province of Black Marsh and were xenophobic, killing foreigners they encountered. They were reclusive and were never seen outside of the inner swamps of Black Marsh.
Sathasa Nerothren is a Dunmer Healer who lives in Ashanammu.
The is a bullpup assault rifle featured in Call of Duty: Black Ops Cold War and Call of Duty: Mobile.
Selveni Nethri is a Dunmer Necromancer who is trapped inside a spider's web after having been left to die in Southfringe Sanctum by Bashnag and her fellow Spellsword mages.
The Servant of Almalexia is a spectral projection encompassing the knowledge of Almalexia.
The Servant of Sotha Sil is a spectral projection encompassing the knowledge of Sotha Sil.
The Elite Foregrip is an underbarrel attachment featured in Call of Duty: Mobile, available to the BK57 assault rifle.
Severin Charnis is a Breton necromancer and a member of the Daggerfall Covenant. He is the one responsible for raising the buried dead in Skyshroud Barrow.

Sharn gra-Muzgob is an Orsimer healer in the Balmora Mages Guild. She appears to have an unusual interest in human remains. She can teach a number of spells, and can train the Nerevarine in Mysticism, Restoration, and Alteration. She also sells a number of potions.

Shando-ri is an ancient Khajiit spirit and a member of the Order of the Hidden Moon residing at the Ashen Scar in Northern Elsweyr. He holds the sacred artifact the Moonlight Blade, the only way to enter Arum-Khal dark realm.
Dynamic Arms Corp. is a weapon manufacturer in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare.
Sigvatr the Strong is a Nord barbarian who resides near the Iggnir River on the island of Solstheim.
Shulki Shandasi is a Dunmer commoner and lycanthrope residing in Gnisis on Vvardenfell. He is located inside Shandasi's House. He has no unique dialogue.
Shulkunaak is a dragon that appears in . He is involved in the quest "Facing the Dragon" where he reveals to the Fugitive how to defeat Celemaril Light-Bringer.

The are a melee weapon featured in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare II. They were added as part of the Season Six update. The Dual Kamas are also available in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare III as part of the Modern Warfare II content carryover.

Sir Gregory was a member of the old Knights of the Nine. He left his duties to serve in the War of the Red Diamond; however, he was killed in battle. His spirit now protects the Cuirass of the Crusader from those who would misuse its power.
Sir Marley Oris is a Breton spirit found at the Burial Mounds, Glenumbra, in .
Skink-in-Tree's-Shade is an Argonian Sorcerer, and member of the Mages Guild.
The Dravec 45 is a submachine gun featured in Call of Duty: Black Ops 7.
Skelos Undriel is a Bosmer Shadowmage in . He seeks the Star Teeth and guides the Hero on their quest to destroy Pergan Asuul and Umbra'Keth. His fate depends on the actions of the Hero.
Sister Balra is a Reachman werewolf member of the Icereach Coven.

Sorkvild the Raven is a Nord battlemage who resides at the summit of his tower on the outskirts of Dagon Fel, Morrowind. Sorkvild is a hostile necromancer, and is an assassination target during the Imperial Legion quest "Sorkvild the Raven." The Nerevarine can obtain the Clavicus Vile's Masque upon Sorkvild's death. The Masque is a Daedric artifact that provides a constant effect bonus of 30 Fortify Personality.

The ECR Phoenix was an assault rifle that was featured in Call of Duty: Future Warfare. However, when Future Warfare was canceled, the ECR Phoenix was discarded as well, and was never ported to any other future titles.

Snowy Granius is an Imperial Battlemage who resides outside the Dwemer Ruins of Arkngthand. Granius guards the Dwemer bridge outside Arkngthand to stop people from accessing the ruin and will attack the Nerevarine on sight.
Spectral Warhounds are creatures in . Found accompanying spectral Draugr in the Labyrinthian, they attack on sight with a melee bite.

Spriggan Matrons are generally seen within the heavily forested areas and natural caves of Skyrim. They are usually accompanied by one or two spriggans and/or bears or wolves that keep their opponent busy while they swoop in for their attack. They may be identified by their golden halo effect and taller, more muscular form, in contrast to the green halo and slender silhouette of a regular spriggan.

The ESR was a sniper rifle that was featured in Call of Duty: Future Warfare. However, when Future Warfare was canceled, the ESR was discarded as well, and was never ported to any other future titles. In-game, the ESR's Arsenal preview was the same as Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2s Barrett .50cal, and gameplay-wise sported the same look as the Intervention.
Spirit of the Ancient Traveler is an unused undead Nord in . Oddly, he does not have a head, making him one of only two ghosts in the game without one, the other being the Headless Horseman.
Spinner Indinael is a Bosmer and lich located in Ouze, Malabal Tor, in .
Student Endannie is an Altmer member of the Mages Guild residing in the city of Skywatch.
The EGRT-17 is an assault rifle featured in Call of Duty: Black Ops 7. It was added as part of the Season Two update.

Stromgruf the Steady is the Nord who is found in the Grazelands of Vvardenfell, west of Pulk and east of Vassamsi Grotto. He is frozen in place by a spell cast by Nerise Venim, and asks for your assistance in getting free.
Sybille Stentor is a Breton vampire in who serves as the Court Wizard of the Blue Palace in Solitude.

Suturah was an advisor to the usurper King Fahara'jad and secretly a practicing Necromancer. Suturah killed all of King Fahara'jad advisors and reanimated them in an attempted assassination of the King, though the attempt failed Suturah did manage to escape. Suturah fled to the eastern portion of Hammerfell where he joined the ranks of the Order of the Black Worm. With the help of the Order, Suturah raised an army of undead Ra-Netu and began to march on Sentinel; but before Suturah reached Sentinel his army was ambushed by the Ash'abah tribe and was slain by the headman of the tribe Marimah. Decades later, however, Suturah's children Uwafa, Alasan and Shiri formed the Withered Hand, a cabal of necromancers who sought to finish what their father started and take over the Alik'r and transform it into a kingdom of death. Shiri would ultimately use the power of Ansei Wards and her own life to raise Suturah as a Lich, but he is ultimately slain by a member of the Ash'abah and their allies.

*EM1- A Heavy Weapon featured in Call of Duty: Advanced Warfare. *EPM3- A Heavy Weapon featured in Call of Duty: Advanced Warfare. *EMP - A kill/scorestreak featured in several games. *EMZ - A type of zombie that appears in Exo Zombies. *EM Troop - A type of soldier featured in Exo Survival. *EM Drone - A type of drone featured in Exo Survival.

Talvas Fathryon is a Dunmer conjurer and Neloth's apprentice. He can be found in Tel Mithryn. Talvas strives constantly to impress Neloth, to prove himself as an apprentice who is worth the time and effort to teach. Unfortunately, it seems that almost all of his efforts are in vain, as Neloth berates him at every turn and constantly considers him inept. The Dragonborn first encounters Talvas during one such attempt to prove himself, trying to perform Conjure Ash Guardian—a particularly tricky spell that only Neloth had mastered at the time. Talvas fails to do it properly, which results in the "From the Ashes" quest.

Teekeeus is an Argonian Wizard and the Head of the Chorrol Mages Guild. Teekeeus and Earana have a long-standing feud that goes back to their days as apprentices at the Arcane University. Teekeeus also starts the Chorrol Mages Guild Recommendation quest.
Telis Salvani is a Dunmer healer who resides at the Temple in Balmora.

The F-15 Eagle is a single seat, twin engine, all weather, air superiority and tactical fighter designed to gain and maintain air superiority in aerial combat, as well as conduct air-to-ground airstrikes and tactical bombing missions.
Tarerane is an Altmer nightblade and vampire who resides in the vampire hideout of Ashmelech.

Thalmor Soldiers are male and female Altmer members of the Thalmor, usually adorned in full Elven armor and Elven weapons. For spells, Thalmor Soldiers use Bound Sword and Flames. They are found in a duo or trio, often accompanied by a Thalmor Wizard or a Thalmor Justiciar.
Teres Arothan is a Dunmer Healer who resides in Dissapla Mine.
The Enfield is a fully-automatic bullpup assault rifle featured in Call of Duty: Black Ops.
Temylda was a High King of Skyrim, and was the most trusted advisor to the previous King, Irthvyd the Impassive. He bested several Jarls in single combat before being named King.

The Cursed One is a Wraith miniboss found in the Vaults of Madness. He is surrounded by several generic Skeletons, but is otherwise not notable besides his Drain Life attack (will likely kill a party member if rest of the group continues to attack after the boss's dialogue).
The Emerald Princess is a Breton ghost found in the Burial Mounds.
The Experimental Fighter Jet is a controllable vehicle in Call of Duty: Black Ops (Nintendo DS), mission "Stolen Wings".
Thiirchel is a Bosmer battlemage and criminal hiding in Hrota Cave, located north of Anvil.

Thervam Drelas is a hostile Dunmer battlemage and bandit who resides in Yasamsi. He lives there with three other smugglers, Dudley, Larisus Dergius, and Ralos Othrenim. He has murdered the innocent Julielle Aumine.

Thjordic Four-Thumbed is a Nord who has cast a faulty illusion spell that makes him appear to be an undead skeleton. He can be found in the Mournhold Outlaws Refuge, sitting in an ashes pit with mushrooms growing out of it.

Extra Attachment is a perk featured in Call of Duty: Ghosts. It allows the player to equip a third attachment to their primary weapon and a second attachment to their secondary, similarly to the Primary Gunfighter and Secondary Gunfighter wildcards from Call of Duty: Black Ops II, Call of Duty: Advanced Warfare and Call of Duty: Black Ops III. Even with Extra Attachment equipped, the same limit of one attachment per attachment group still applies. Extra Attachment is most useful on multi-purpose weapons, such as assault rifles or light machine guns. One could, for example, add Armor-Piercing rounds to a light machine gun already equipped with a Foregrip and an optical attachment, to add extra punch against armor and pointstreaks, without compromising the accuracy of the weapon. The perk is less useful on more specialized weapons, such as Shotguns or Pistols, as they generally don't require more than two attachments to be effective. It is completely ineffective on the Riot Shield, which is restricted to mod attachments, and the VKS, which only has two groups of attachments. Extra Attachment is most useful on classes using a primary and secondary weapon, with the perk granting one extra attachment to each weapon. Extra Attachment is required to complete the operation "Clueless" which requires 200 kills with Akimbo + ACOG Scope .44 Magnums. The Torturer is an elder Imperial Legionnaire in Helgen. He wears a set of Imperial Light Armor, with the exception of the helmet, which is replaced with a unique Torturer's Hood. He also carries a Steel Dagger; however, he uses Destruction Magic in combat instead.
Tussi is a Dunmer Healer living in Zainab Camp. Tussi buys and sells potions and ingredients. She only carries 75 .

Undead Akaviri Soldiers are skeletons that died long ago during the invasion on Cyrodiil, who now roam the Serpent's Trail. Undead Akaviri Soldiers were men who lived long ago. Like other skeletons, they may be hit back but reform immediately. They can be found in Sancre Tor, guarding Tiber Septim's tome. There are rumored to be small clans of "true" Akaviri still on Tamriel, though the details are sketchy.
Eyeballs Personalization Pack is a downloadable content package available for Call of Duty: Ghosts. It contains a weapon camo, reticle, a player background and a player patch.

Uriel Septim V was the seventeenth ruler of the Empire of Tamriel. He inherited the throne from his father, Cephorus Septim II, in 3E 268. His reign was marked by several ambitious conquests, the last of which was to the continent of Akavir. He is regarded as the best warrior Emperor since his ancestor Tiber Septim.

Urmuk One Hand was an Orc warrior who served with Radhasa in kidnapping Prince Attrebus. He gained the name of One Hand after losing his hand, and instead of a hand, had an iron ball fixed to his stump.
Urjorad is a Khajiit Healer who died in Ashalmimilkala. He was a healer and member of the Imperial Cult.

Extinction Personalization Pack is a downloadable content package available for Call of Duty: Ghosts. It contains a weapon camo, reticle, a player background and a player patch. Urtiso Faryon: Sorcerer is a small shop in northeastern Sadrith Mora that is owned, operated, and inhabited by Urtiso Faryon, a Dunmer sorcerer who offers spells and custom spellmaking services.

Vampire Mistwalker is a type of vampire in that is encountered randomly throughout Skyrim. Their race is radiant. Their Vampiric Drain absorbs both health and stamina from their targets, making them much more dangerous than their Fledgling and Blooded counterparts

Valdimar is a Nord sorcerer in Hjaalmarch. He is appointed Housecarl when the Dragonborn becomes the Thane of Hjaalmarch. He can be found at Highmoon Hall, or at Windstad Manor once the Dragonborn has bought the deed from the Jarl.

The Exo Shield is an Exo Ability in Call of Duty: Advanced Warfare. It allows the player to deploy a shield around themselves to protect against attacks for a short time. It is functionally the same as the Heavy Shield, including the ability to melee with the shield as long as the ability is in use. It lasts for four seconds without Overcharged and five seconds with it. A large "02" and the words "Electrified Ballistic Mesh" can be seen on the front and back of the shield, respectively. In campaign, it is available alongside Overdrive in all the missions where the Specialist exo type is used: "Atlas", "Traffic", "Aftermath", "Manhunt", "Utopia", "Sentinel" and "Bio Lab".

Vadelen Indothan is a Dunmer found at the Five Claws Inn in Woodhearth. Unlike many of his people, he despises the practice of slavery and expresses his wishes to be a Khajiit, whom he believes to be his true people. In that goal, he attempted to brew a specific potion that would have allowed him to become one but it failed and instead turned him into an Argonian.
Varona Nelas is a Dunmer sorcerer who resides in the cave of Assumanu. She has obtained a token given to a Buoyant Armiger via a secret abolitionist, who would like to have it returned to them.

Variner's Ghost is a unique ancestor ghost in the . He is found in Old Mournhold's Temple Sewers during the quest "The Black Dart Gang". The former companion of Narisa Adus, he was killed by The Black Dart Gang in an attempt to prevent her from being harmed. Since his death he has been visiting Narisa at night.

Exo Soldier is an exo upgrade in Call of Duty: Advanced Warfare in Exo Zombies on the maps Outbreak, Infection, Carrier and Descent. It costs 1,750 Credits. It has similar effects to Gung-Ho and Fast Hands, allowing the player to shoot while sprinting and sliding. It also increases weapon swap speed and hip fire accuracy (similar to Deadshot Daiquiri). Unlike multiplayer, when ADS, the player will not be slowed down for a few seconds. The upgrade also affects the chain gun on the XS1 Goliath in Descent, as the player will be able to shoot the chain gun while sprinting when in the Goliath.

Vorian Direnni was the author of the book De Rerum Dirennis and a member of the Direnni Bloodline. At the time of the book's writing, he was 611 years of age. Although never fighting with a sword, He was a noted wizard and was alive during the "chaotic years" of the Second Era. Vorian never had any child of his own.
Vulyne Rothari is a Dunmer healer in Morrowind. She can be found in the Ginith Ancestral Tomb.
Vix is a baby snow fox that can be acquired by an adopted child as a pet in .

Extra Armory Slots is a micro-DLC in Call of Duty: Advanced Warfare. It gives the player an extra 120 slots in their Armory for weapon variants and character gear. This can be downloaded up to 9 times (through separate purchases) to have even more Armory slots.
Vladolfr the Strong is a Nord armorer residing in the city of Mournhold, Deshaan. He can be found selling his wares at the Artisans Craftworks.

Werewolf Brute are feral Werewolves. They can be encountered as random encounters in Silver Hand bases from level 12 and upward. They will attack the Dragonborn and any followers on sight even if they are in Beast Form.

The Wood Elves are a race hailing from the province of Valenwood. They are a people of the forests, matching their features to all that is found growing in the green woods of their homeland. They are known to be extremely agile and quick. Bosmer receive their (level / 3) as a bonus to hit and damage with any bow weapon. They are well suited towards any class, although their nimbleness serves them best in any art involving thievery.

Explosive Touch (Referred to as "Overcharge" in the game files) is a power-up that appears in the Exo Zombies maps Carrier and Descent, replacing Hyper-Damage. It is represented by a star. While this power-up is active, Zombies will be instantly killed if they make contact with the player.

Wonshala Keriayn is a Dark Seducer and commander of Dagon's Spider Daedra. She has a piece of the voidguide, and will exchange it for Scourge, an enchanted mace blessed by Malacath. She will drain half the Apprentice's current health if they anger her.
Yakin Bael is a Dunmer healer and trainer of Mysticism, Alteration, and Restoration. He can be found in the Vos Chapel in Vos.
Wulfgar is an Elder Nord, and one of the Greybeards. As for the other Greybeards, save for Arngeir, his voice is too powerful to be heard by common people, so he does not speak.

Ensign is an achievement/trophy in Call of Duty: Advanced Warfare in Exo Zombies. It requires the player to reach round 10 on Carrier. Ensign XBOX One Achievement Image AW.png|XBOX One Achievement Image
Wunalz is an Argonian ghost found in the Temple of Mourning Springs after the quest "Tears of the Two Moons" has been completed.

Yaremanwe is an Altmer ghost found in the Temple of Mourning Springs after the "Tears of the Two Moons" quest has been completed, and the ghosts have returned to the temple. She cannot be directly interacted with.
Yamanu-ko is a Khajiit necromancer and archmage of the Blackcaster Mages Guild. She is found at the top of the Apex Tower in Elinhir.

Exo Stockpile is an exo upgrade in Call of Duty: Advanced Warfare in the game mode Exo Zombies. Introduced in the map Carrier, Exo Stockpile increases the amount of ammunition players can hold in their weapons by 20%, and the amount of lethal grenades and tactical grenades that players can carry by one grenade each type. Players also receive two grenades of each type instead of just one per round.

Ygfa is a Nord Healer who can be found selling spells, ingredients and potions at Fort Pelagiad. She is a member of the Imperial Cult, and an established Healer Service. As such, asking her about diseases yields a lot of information about them. She is able to identify all sixteen common diseases and all four blight diseases that exist in Morrowind.
Zanmulk Sammalamus is a Dunmer healer living in Gnisis in the West Gash.
Yngol's Shade is a unique spectral draugr found in Yngol Barrow.
The Erad (capitalized as the ERAD in pre-release) is a Mashimo energy submachine gun featured in Call of Duty: Infinite Warfare and Call of Duty: Heroes.
Zal'ik is a powerful Skeleton found inside the ruins of Shada's Tear.

Zabeth is an undead Sword-Disciple of the Rahni'Za, School of Warriors who committed suicide when Abelazar attacked the school. He can be found on his knees, kneeling over a dead Sword-Disciple's corpse with a note next to him.

Zumog Phoom is a powerful Orsimer necromancer serving under Euraxia Tharn. Initially, he acts as Euraxia's advisor and strategist, and provides her with large amounts of reinforcements in the form of necromancers and undead soldiers. However, his main aim is to put Cadwell the Betrayer back together and gain favor with the dragons. He and his necromancers abandon Euraxia shortly before her death.
The Eraser is a energy-based heavy weapon featured in Call of Duty: Infinite Warfare; it is available as a Payload for FTL.

The aspiring Pint-Sized Phantom, also known as Casper or the Pint-Sized Phantom spectator, is a new recruit within the Pint-Sized Phantoms, as well as the only non-hostile member of the faction, . He appears only when The Slasher seasonal content is active.
Billy Peabody is a ghoul child living in the Commonwealth in 2287.
Doc is an initiate in the Brotherhood of Steel. He is an all-around combatant, but is best kept to the rear of combat to provide much needed medical support.

Evelynn "Boats" Sotomura is a bridge officer stationed on the Retribution. She served as the carrier's boatswain. She comes from a family with a proud history of naval service. Her ancestors served in the military, so she proceeded to follow in their footsteps. She graduated at the top of her naval academy class and has provided distinguished service to SATO forces throughout her career. She presumably survived the events of Operation Blood Storm, as she was one of the few named characters to make it to the SetDef shipyard, along with Nora Salter, Sean Brooks and Erwin Kloos.
Evan Holyfeld is a boxer fighting in the Jungle Gym in 2241.
The extremely broken Securitron is a robot character in season two of the Fallout TV series.

Erwin Kloos was a Deck Handler aboard the UNSA carrier Retribution for outfitting, refuelling and launch prepping Jackal fighter craft under the supervision of Air Boss Laura Gibson. Kloos was aboard the SDF Destroyer during the final mission in Call of Duty: Infinite Warfare. He is one of the four surviving crew members of the SATO Retribution along with Nora Salter, Evelynn "Boats" Sotomura and Sean Brooks.

Giant kangaroo rats are creatures found in the Texas Wasteland. They could be found in the wasteland roaming the freeway system between Lubbock and Lone Star, where among other mutant critters they are a threat to unfortunate travelers.
Preacher Levenson (alternatively labeled as "Haven Church EyeBot" in the game files) is a named Eyebot flying randomly throughout Appalachia.

Exclusion Zone Camouflage is a type of weapon camouflage skin featured in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare Remastered.

Marshall's place is a building in New Canaan. The glowing ghoul Mormon named Marshall can be found here. Marshall is dangerous not because he is violent, but because he is highly radioactive. Apostle Jude comes here once a day to talk to Marshall, who is slowly dying.
"Steel" Mark Torrance is a boxer in New Reno's Jungle Gym in 2241.
Mike "The Masticator" is a heavyweight boxing champion in 2241.
Extra Equipment is a suit upgrade in the campaign of Call of Duty: Infinite Warfare.
Melody K. Larkin was a senior member of the Responders assigned to combat training and the leader of the Fire Breathers.
Morte, born Mortimer Rictusgrin, is a floating skull, and actually not a Mimir. He can be met in the special encounter Morte.

The Ethereal Weapon Kit is a Rare weapon kit available in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare Remastered. It is available for the shotguns in the game, and consists of a black and gray design with an image of a skull on it.

Pestilence is one of the Four Horsemen of the Post Apocalypse, found in a special encounter in 2197. Pestilence, like the other horsemen, will stand around the campfire and argue. It's not like he has anything important to do, the human race has already been effectively destroyed.
Pint-Sized Phantoms are hostile members of the Pint-Sized Phantoms faction in Appalachia. They appear in The Slasher seasonal content.

Raul Alfonso Tejada is a Mexican ghoul mechanic and former legendary gunslinger from Mexico City. By 2281, he is a prisoner of the State of Utobitha at Black Mountain in the Mojave Wasteland. He is a possible companion of the Courier.

Everlast is a Common gun perk in Call of Duty: Infinite Warfare found exclusively upon energy based weapon variants. The effect is similar to the Fusion Mag attachment, in that a weapon with the perk will generate energy ammo, even when not active.

Robert Joseph "RJ" MacCready is the adolescent mayor of the child-exclusive settlement of Little Lamplight in the Capital Wasteland in 2277. By 2287, the grown-up MacCready is working as a mercenary in the Commonwealth, selling his services from the backroom of the Third Rail in Goodneighbor. He is a possible companion of the Sole Survivor.
Scott "Scoot" Conroy is a wendigo living in the sunken church in Appalachia.
Shepherd was a super mutant warlord residing in the Capital Wasteland.

The Entangler is a special wonder weapon featured in the Call of Duty: Infinite Warfare Zombies mode. It appears in all of the Ghosts 'N Skulls machines and can also be used outside of the machines in The Beast From Beyond, where it plays a pivotal role in the map's main easter egg.
The Smiling Man, also known as Indrid Cold, is a mysterious person randomly encountered in Appalachia .

Subject 46 is a slave for the Mordinos, being used to refine Jet at the Stables in 2241. During testing, Subject 46 had a heart attack, causing the scientists to restrict the doses to six times a day.

The Homing Missiles, referred to as the AT6 Missiles and S.W.A.R.M. Missiles in campaign, are a weapon for the XS1 Goliath in Call of Duty: Advanced Warfare. In multiplayer, they are equipped when the Homing Rockets module is added to the Goliath. They fire at enemy targets that are highlighted in red in the HUD. They fire four missiles at a time. However, not all missiles will always impact the target, as they may be impeded by obstacles, making it possible that one burst will not kill. Once used, the player has to wait 10 seconds before the homing missiles are ready again.

The 3-C SOLDIER Operator is an enemy in Final Fantasy VII Remake and "Episode INTERmission". They are members of Shinra Electric Power Company's elite fighting force known as SOLDIER. The third class SOLDIERs are deployed to protect the Shinra Building in Chapter 16, "The Belly of the Beast", and in Chapter 2, "Covert Ops" in "Episode INTERmission". In the base game, they are also fought on the Collapsed Sector 7 Plate on the way there in Chapter 15, "The Day Midgar Stood Still". __TOC__

The Ananta are a race of lamia-like beastmen in Final Fantasy XIV: Stormblood. They are indigenous to the mountains near Ala Mhigo and are solely female. Their affiliated primal is Lakshmi, the Lady of Bliss, whom they worship as a creator goddess. The Ananta are said to have existed since the time of ancient Allag, and are known for their skill in spell and gemcraft. They are divided by two sister tribes: the Vira, who see Lakshmi as an embodiment of freedom, and the Qalyana, who consider their goddess to personify transcending beauty, which they emulate while ignoring everything else around them.

Ark Dragon is an enemy from Final Fantasy VII fought in the Mythril Mine and in the sixth round of the Battle Square before the player obtains the Tiny Bronco. When fought in the Battle Square its stats are enhanced with double the normal HP and its Attack and Magic Attack are increased by 25%.
The Hound is an unmanned anti-personnel ground vehicle used by Winslow Accord and the CDP in Call of Duty: Black Ops III.
Babus Swain is Mewt Randell's nu mou assistant from Final Fantasy Tactics Advance. An experienced mage, he will do anything to protect Mewt.

Barret is a playable character in Final Fantasy VII. He is the first party member to join Cloud, accompanying him after Cloud's first battle at the beginning of the game. He is a ranged attacker, using a machine gun mounted in place of his amputated arm. He is a strong physical attacker early on, though due to his ultimate weapon Missing Score, whose damage depends on the AP of equipped Materia, he is later best built towards magical damage (or Command Materia that requires a lot of AP to master). Barret's ultimate weapon can also overflow damage. Barret is the hardest date option to get for Cloud in a scene in Gold Saucer during "Secret Date".
Bite Bug is an enemy in Final Fantasy VIII. A bug monster that flies, this pesky blue insect is one of the first monster types the player will encounter.

The Hunter Tank is a unit in Call of Duty: Heroes. It is available at Heavy Machine Facility level three. They have one of the longest attack ranges allowing them to deal great damage while avoiding most defensive structures.

Blaze Toad is an enemy from Final Fantasy IV: The After Years. It is not a very powerful enemy, but can prove to be a nuisance with its Toad spell. It is recommended to bring along plenty of Maiden's Kisses, and to try and defeat the enemies in one shot if possible.

Blood Soul is an enemy in Final Fantasy VIII commonly found on the Galbadian continent. It is a small flying undead enemy that inflicts the party with Zombie and then uses curative spells on them to deal damage.

The Bolt Drake is an enemy from Final Fantasy X-2 that can be found in the Thunder Plains, Bikanel Desert, Mt. Gagazet, and Cloisters 24-26 of the Via Infinito. It uses Kusariqqu's model from Final Fantasy X.

Hitman is a Legendary gun perk in Call of Duty: Infinite Warfare, found upon certain weapon variants. It allows the player to earn a bonus to their Payload meter when killing all players on the enemy team. The enemy team must have 4 or more players for Hitman to activate.

Bronwell is a character of War of the Visions: Final Fantasy Brave Exvius. A missionary of the Sanctum Curia hailing from the Tessera continent south of Ardra, she is capable of both sensing and purging the corruption caused by the Crystals' magic. Having come to Ardra together with Shelva to spread the teachings of the Crystal faith, she is surprised to hear that Sadali, a fellow missionary who was believed to have gone missing after coming to Ardra, has in fact established a Sanctum of the Crystal faith already. Being told of his sinister machinations, Bronwell decides to infiltrate the church and investigate him.
Buel is an enemy in Final Fantasy VIII. It is a physically weak flying monster that uses various magic.
The Changer, also known as the Swapper, is an enemy from Final Fantasy II. This monster owes its name to its mastery of the Swap IV skill, which switches the HP and MP of the Changer with its target.
Hurl is an Epic gun perk featured in Call of Duty: Infinite Warfare. It is exclusive to the Axe's Epic Headsman variant. It allows the Axe to be thrown and picked up like a Throwing Knife.

Corses are floating, undead corpses that can strike instant fear in the heart of any unwary adventurer. Found mainly in the Attohwa Chasm, these undead are solitary and reclusive, with less than a dozen able to be identified at any given time. Their reclusive nature is less noticeable at night, when these monsters come out of their hiding spots. Not only are corses able to silence their opponents, but they can even temporarily charm them and force the charmed attacker to instead attack his or her own party members. For this reason alone, all adventurers should be cautious when approaching. To the victors fall a few interesting items. The bracelets and robes worn by the corse can be picked off of their now twice-defeated bodies. These items can be desynthesized into precious metals and gemstones (in the case of the bracelets) or cloths and threads (in the case of the robes). Of even more interest are the iolite that all corses carry. These blue jewels are only found on the corse, and are an item requested by Bluffnix to expand an adventurer's inventory.
Cyan is a playable character in Final Fantasy VI. He is a Samurai who can unleash Bushido attacks by charging up a secondary ATB gauge—the longer Cyan charges, the more powerful the attack he uses.
Flame Flan is an enemy from Final Fantasy X. It is found in the Calm Lands appearing with other fiends. It is a red gelatinous monster with flaming eyes and insides.
High Rider is a Common gun perk in Call of Duty: Infinite Warfare. It grants the player a reduced hip fire spread when jumping in the air with the weapon.

The Flyer Mage, also known as the MageFlyer, is an enemy from Final Fantasy III. It can be found in the Cave of the Circle. Physical attacks are useless in fighting them as the player is forced to fight under Mini status, and therefore it is recommended to use non-physical attacks, such as magic. Aero and Aeroga are best in defeating them as they are weak to Wind. An alternative is to have a Dark Knight use Darkness or a Geomancer use Terrain.

s 2013 release.]] Gaelicat , sometimes called Ghilacat or Cait Sith, is a recurring creature in the Final Fantasy series introduced in Final Fantasy V. It appears as a cat wearing a flying contraption with a bell attached. Its signature attack is Cat Scratch. Commonly, a stronger variation called Flying Killer can also be found.

Ghrahs have an elemental alignment indicated by the color of their glowing core. Ghrahs appear in 4 different forms: Ball (Black Mage), Bird (Thief), Spider (Warrior), and Humanoid (Paladin). Ghrahs will still cast magic in any form, however. Most Ghrahs alternate between Ball and one other form particular to that Ghrah every 60-75 seconds. In the "Ball" form, Ghrahs are not aggressive. When not in Ball form, Ghrahs aggro by True Sound. Neither form links. High Velocity is a weapon perk featured in the Nazi Zombies mode in Call of Duty: WWII. It gives the weapon increased bullet penetration, which can also be stacked with the effects of the Full Metal Jacket attachment. Currently, this perk is found only on the Chiller variant of the Gewehr 43.

The Giza Rabbit, called Happy Bunny in the BradyGames guide, is a beast/dreamhare-type enemy in Final Fantasy XII. It is not a threat, and is docile until attacked. It is found on the Giza Plains during the Dry season. While docile, a Giza Rabbit may cast Cure on any character or other monster nearby if significantly hurt. The Giza Rabbits in the northern areas of Giza Plains have slightly more HP than the Giza Rabbits that dwell in the southern areas. Once attacked, they will run around the area, possibly attracting the attention of nearby enemies. After running away, it casts Protect and Cure onto itself. They may engage in battle if surrounded.

The Gold Warrior, also known as the GoldWarr., is an enemy from Final Fantasy III. It is found in Goldor Manor. They are relatively powerful, but are among the weaker enemies found in the manor. Physical attacks work well enough in defeating them.

The Gorgias, also known as Tusker, is an enemy in Final Fantasy VI. It can counter most physical attacks, and its special attack, Gore, is powerful. A good strategy is to have Terra cast Fire spells and Edgar use his Auto Crossbow.

The Holda (referred to as the Nazi Axe by the Notebook) is one of the three special melee weapons featured in the Call of Duty: WWII Nazi Zombies map The Shadowed Throne. It is a golden axe with a black handle with the logo of the Ahnenerbe emblazoned on a golden plate attached to it, with the Iron Cross placed on the head. The entire axe pulsates with Geistkraft energy.

The Gorgonopsid Ω is an enemy in Lightning Returns: Final Fantasy XIII. It is a Last One that appears when there is only one Gorgonopsid left in the game after 80 of their species have been felled. Its Virulent Breath can be guarded with a strong shield. If it uses War Cry, The player can use Brave Thief to steal its buff.
Halicarnassus , also known as Halycanos or Harikalnasson, is a recurring boss in the Final Fantasy series. They are typically a powerful humanoid spellcaster fond of inflicting the Toad status.
Hexadragon is an enemy in Final Fantasy VIII, a peculiar six-legged dragon with six eyes. The Hexadragon has an elemental defense towards Fire.

The Hilt of Barbarossa is one of the three main pieces of the Sword of Barbarossa. Hidden away underneath the town of Mittelburg, it would suspended in the air for centuries by an unknown force before the seal was broken by the MFAA, who sought to collect the hilt after receiving information from Klaus Fischer. Prior to its recovery by the MFAA, the Ahnenerbe utilized the hilt for years as a type of power source, siphoning off the seemingly infinite amount of Geistkraft energy within it to create the undead and powerful weaponry in order to help the Nazis combat the Allied Powers and win World War II. As later revealed by Peter Straub, he had siphoned enough energy to revive the entire Wehrmacht ten times over.

The Immortal Lions, more commonly known simply as the Immortals, are a group of Blue Mages that serve in the employ of the Empire of Aht Urhgan functionally as an elite guard in Final Fantasy XI. They are stationed around areas controlled by the empire, including in Aht Urhgan itself as well as at each of the various staging points controlled by the Empire. The Immortals were founded after the Chimera Rebellion, an occasion on which the Emperor's son was assassinated. The Emperor then confronted the alchemists responsible with making the Chimerae, charging them with finding a means to defeat the creatures. The Alchemists, after many failed attempts, concluded that the guards themselves would have to become monsters. At first, it was a disaster. Attempts to graft animal parts and limbs to humans resulted in gruesome and horrific outcomes when most of the test subjects' bodies rejected the grafts. Finally, the Alchemists found a brutal way to bind the essence of a monster directly to the human spirit. Thus, Blue Magic was born, and so were the elite Immortal Guards. It came with a price, however: no known Immortal lived to the end of his natural lifespan. Also, using Blue Magic put enormous strain on the user, usually putting them through a great deal of pain. Another ghastly side effect is when the spirit of the beast bound to the Blue Mage's soul begins to corrupt the mage's mind. Gradually, the Blue Mage goes mad, and then loses all human behaviors and qualities. Finally, it

Jusqua is a playable character in Final Fantasy: The 4 Heroes of Light. A young boy with a cool, mysterious aura, he joins Brandt's group, but considers him a rival. Although the game follows a job system, Jusqua is depicted as a staff-wielding magic user in official artwork. He is met in the North Caves.

.]] The lamia is a recurring creature in the Final Fantasy series, first appearing in Final Fantasy II. It is a serpentine demon known for its signature Entice and Slap abilities, which can inflict status effects like Charm, Confuse, Sap, and Paralysis.

The Hitchcock M9 is an assault rifle featured in the Zombies mode of Call of Duty: Black Ops 4, obtained from the Mystery Box in all Zombies maps. When upgraded via Pack-a-Punch Machine, it becomes the Walking Nightmare with the magazine size increased to 70 rounds and its ammo reserve increased to 420. The weapon now uses explosive rounds, and can hurt multiple zombies and make crawlers.

Lamia Matriarch is a Soul of Rebirth enemy in Final Fantasy II. She is a palette swap of the Lamia, meant to resemble the Lamia species introduced in Final Fantasy IV, and is a somewhat dangerous enemy when first encountered; she can inflict Confuse on party members with her Charm IX attack, as well as inflict Sleep with her physical attack. Their Blizzard XII spell is hardly noticeable compared to the other two abilities. They can be dealt with in a variety of ways, but should be taken care of either first or last, depending on which enemies they come with. If they come with Cait Siths, it is advised to defeat the Cait Siths first. The Lamia Matriarch can drop the powerful Ribbon, making it a useful enemy to farm. They can also provide the Thunder Spear, which grants the party free access to to the spell Thunder XVI.

Latov is a 40-year-old Clavat from Final Fantasy Crystal Chronicles: Ring of Fates. He is the father of the twins Yuri and Chelinka, and husband of their mother, Aleria. He is a skilled swordsman and once commanded the Royal Guard of Rebena Te Ra, working closely with Meeth, Alhanalem and Aleria. He took care of Yuri and Chelinka in Villa and created Rela Cyel with Alhanalem and Meeth. Latov's willpower is strong.

Locke is a playable character in Final Fantasy VI. He is playable throughout the World of Balance and is required for several storyline segments, and is an optional recruit in the World of Ruin. His skillset aligns with the Thief class, but his actual job title is "Adventurer", reflecting he is a bit more physically adept than Thieves usually are in other titles.

The Hellfire is a Specialist Weapon featured in Call of Duty: Black Ops 4. It is usable in the Zombies Aether Story maps Blood of the Dead, Classified, Alpha Omega and Tag der Toten. At Level 1, the Hellfire functions similarly to the Purifier, acting as a Flamethrower that can damage any enemies. After each kill with the flamethrower, the player also gains additional Armor. At Level 2, the Blast Vent ability is unlocked, allowing the player to release a burst of pressurized air, sending enemies flying. At Level 3, the Infernal Tempest ability is unlocked, allowing the player to create a tornado of flames that wipe out any enemies in its path.

Mad Toad is an enemy type from Final Fantasy Mystic Quest. It is the strongest toad-type monster, and common throughout the Giant Tree. Mad Toad can inflict many status ailments upon the party, and counters with Poison-touch when physically attacked. The first phase of the battle has the Mad Toad squat and glare at the opponent. Upon losing a significant amount of health, it falls on its back and has a white cross bandage on its stomach.
Manhole is an enemy from Final Fantasy VII, fought in Sector 8 of Midgar during "Mako Cannon Rampage". When they hide underground, they cannot be targeted.

Marielle is a minor character in Final Fantasy VII Remake: Picturing the Past, mentioned and named in Final Fantasy VII Remake Traces of Two Pasts. She was Aerith Gainsborough and Ifalna's caretaker in the Shinra Building, and the mother of Aerith's childhood playmate, Lonny. Marielle was responsible for the laundry and chores for Ifalna and Aerith. As well as being paid for the job herself, her son Lonny was also paid, although he did not learn this until he was older and more responsible with money. When Geddie Bach arrived at 10 AM in the morning to pick up Ifalna, Lonny kept Aerith preoccupied the rest of the day. Marielle was present when Aerith's powers were awakened. After embellishing a story about encountering a monster, Lonny drew a wererat he had seen, egged on by Marielle. The drawing caused Aerith to be lost in thought staring at it, as she then grabbed the pen and pad and drew faces, flowers, trees, animals, and a number of images that began pouring into her head. Geddie and Professor Hojo then stepped in, declaring Aerith had awakened. Marielle apologized, realizing what would happen to Aerith thereafter.
The Home Wrecker is a melee weapon that was added to Call of Duty: Black Ops 4 with Patch 1.16. It can be obtained by obtaining the Triple Play bundle for 2800 CODPoints.
The Mega Parasite, also known the Lifesucker, is an enemy from Final Fantasy II. Its attacks may cause Amnesia. Its arsenal includes two powerful sapping attacks, Osmose X and Drain XVI.
The Mini Blue is an enemy in Final Fantasy IV: The After Years. They serve as guardians in the Tower of Trials for Leonora to practice her Black Magic skills.
.]] Mini Dragon , also known as MiniDragon or Baby-D, is a recurring enemy in the Final Fantasy series. They are typically diminutive wingless dragons that attack in packs.
Isabelle DuFontaine was a French resistance fighter featured in Call of Duty 3. She appears to be second in command, right after Pierre LaRoche of the Marquis.

The Mystery Ninja is an enemy from Final Fantasy VII. She attacks the party in random encounters around the world map in forest areas, and her level and stats increase with the party's. Encountering the Mystery Ninja is needed to recruit Yuffie.

Negator is a boss in Final Fantasy X. It is a machina fought in the Crawler battle at Lake Macalania. It stops the use of magic and summons. The Negator model is reused for Picket in Final Fantasy X-2.

The Ologhai, also known as the Olog-Hai, is an enemy from Final Fantasy III. Like most enemies in the Sunken Cave in the 3D versions, it is Water-based and thus weak to Lightning. In the NES version, they are overpowered, having a level of 55—ten levels higher than the dungeon's average—so they are powerful with their physical attacks and must be dealt with quickly.
Corporal Joe Robinson is a crew member in Sam Rivers' Sherman Tank who warns that a building is being held by Germans and needs to be cleared for the 87th Infantry. He uses a Thompson as his weapon.

Strago is a playable character in Final Fantasy VI. He is a Blue Mage, able to mimic the magical attacks of monsters. He joins the party late in the World of Balance before the game shifts to the World of Ruin.

Susanoo is a water-elemental Eidolon that appears in Final Fantasy Dimensions II. The signet can be obtained for Parai to equip as the first-time completion reward for the "Attack System" side quest in Present Westa Outskirts in chapter 4-1. The Susanoo signet provides average boosts to HP and attack, but provides subpar boosts for other stats. In the original free-to-play versions of the game, Susanoo was a water-elemental signet that could only be obtained through the game's summon draw shop. However, He taught the Ame-no-Murakumo ability instead of the Shock ability. In the premium versions of the game, Susanoo's Ame-no-Murakumo abilities were removed from the game and replaced with the Shock ability from the Ark summon. Susanoo is an SS rank summon and can be equipped by any party member.

The Swordking is a seeq Viking in Final Fantasy Tactics A2: Grimoire of the Rift. He boasts of being indomitable but that is only because he turns anyone who opposes him to stone. He appears in the quest "Show of Strength", and travels with two bangaa, a Defender, and a Templar. They immobilize and disable his target. Swordking and his group are encountered by Ghi Yelgi and Clan Gully. When he is finally defeated, he turns himself to stone with his sword.

The , abbreviated as the Kar98k, is a German bolt-action rifle featured in every game of the Call of Duty series set during World War II, as well as appearing in the Rezurrection map pack or the Prestige or Hardened version of Call of Duty Black Ops in Zombies mode, and in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare, Call of Duty: Mobile and Call of Duty: Modern Warfare III. It is used by German soldiers and is usable by the player but is rarely seen in use by other troops of the Allied forces. It is also briefly seen in Call of Duty: Black Ops 6.
The Tako Luka is an enemy in Final Fantasy IV: The After Years. He is fought in the Developers' Office, and cannot be damaged by any attacks.

The Huntsman is a mini-boss in Final Fantasy VII Remake. He is a Shinra infantry equipped with a blazing red riot shield and a stun baton. His shield repels all frontal physical attacks. He is fought in the end of Chapter 2, "Fateful Encounters", as Cloud alone while he is maneuvering through the chaotic streets of Midgar. The Huntsman is later fought at the Corneo Colosseum during "Two-Person Team vs. Slum Outlaws".

Princess Tilika Tawantyn is a ten-year-old half Selkie, half Clavat girl from Final Fantasy Crystal Chronicles: Ring of Fates. She is the daughter of King Kolka and the niece of Aleria. Born in Rebena Te Ra, she possesses a power similar to Chelinka due to them being maternal cousins.

The was a German three engine, troop transport-type aircraft used by the Luftwaffe during World War II. It is featured in Call of Duty: Finest Hour, Call of Duty: World War II and Call of Duty: Vanguard.
The Tiny Mage, also known as the TinyMage, is an enemy from Final Fantasy IV. It can be dangerous because it can counter all physical attacks with Hold and all spells with Osmose.
Tredd Furia is a character in Kingsglaive: Final Fantasy XV and a member of the eponymous Kingsglaive. Having gone through extensive training, he is a top-class soldier.

The Trick Sparrow is a flying enemy from Final Fantasy IX. The party can find them in the Treno area overworld on the Mist Continent. Zidane can also fight them during the Festival of the Hunt in Lindblum. They are weak enemies that pose no big threat to the party at the time they are fought.
The is the standard close quarters combat melee weapon featured in various games and media within the Call of Duty series.

Urd Bahamut is a neutral-elemental Eidolon from Final Fantasy Dimensions II. It is an alternate version of Bahamut that can only be equipped by the Deathlord. The summon is automatically obtained when the Deathlord joins the party during the events of the Interlude chapter. Urd Bahamut is a decent signet for the Deathlord when he initially joins the party, providing decent HP and magic stats. The summon's Trine Breath ability for the Deathlord is a decent attack to deal multiple attacks to groups of enemies and deals extra damage to dragon-type enemies. However, the signet's usefulness is eventually outclassed as the player progresses through the game's Eureka arc. In the original free-to-play versions, Urd Bahamut could only be obtained through the game's summon draw shop and could be equipped by any party member. Urd Bahamut was an SS+ rank signet.

The Vampire Lady, also known as the Succubus, is an enemy from Final Fantasy II. She is a very strong undead enemy with quite a few tricks up her sleeve and can be quite hard to beat, even at the moments they are supposed to be fought. Their physical attacks drain HP and they are resistant to every element except for Fire. They can also turn your heroes against each other with the Charm IX spell, put the party to sleep with Sleep XVI, and can inflict Ice-elemental damage with the Blizzard XII spell. The payout for defeating these difficult creatures is, thankfully, quite large. Also, since the Vampire Lady is undead, attacking her with the Blood Sword will heal her and damage the player.

Vanille is a playable character in Final Fantasy XIII who concentrates on casting magic from a distance, as opposed to the close combat style of Lightning and Snow, although her casting animation is slow compared to most other party members. Despite being able to use the Attack command at the start of the game, she cannot use it after Chapter 3 because she does not have the Commando role, which she unlocks in Chapter 10. When the player first acquires Vanille in the Pulse Vestige, she already has three ATB slots, though unable to select magical abilities or utilize paradigm shifts. She's the only one able to fight her Eidolon with five ATB slots as it is possible, albeit difficult, to acquire a third-tier weapon before that. Vanille's victory pose is to throw her rod into the air with a smile, then catch it and fold it into its pouch.

The (or Stuka) is a German dive bomber and ground-attack aircraft used by the Luftwaffe during World War II. When diving toward is target, it had the ability to make a siren-like sound. Stukas are seen in the majority of Call of Duty games set during World War II but are featured prominently in Call of Duty, Call of Duty: Finest Hour, the final level of Call of Duty: United Offensive, Call of Duty: Roads to Victory, Call of Duty 2: Big Red One, Call of Duty 2, and Call of Duty: WWII.
Vita, the Effervescent Diva, is an obtainable character from King's Knight -Wrath of the Dark Dragon-. Her pastime is singing and her talent is breathing underwater.

Wamouracapa are larval stage wamoura in Final Fantasy XI that periodically switch between a curled-up and open form, even when not engaged. When curled up, their special attacks are limited to Cannonball and Heat Barrier. Left alone, these wamouracapa will morph into full-grown wamoura. As with their full-grown relatives, wamouracampa will occasionally drop their cocoon, which be crafted into Wamoura Silk, which is used in a number of high end items.
The Water Elemental (, , or ), also known as the WATER or Aquos, is a recurring enemy in the Final Fantasy series. True to its name, it is an Elemental enemy with a Water affinity.

The is a long Japanese sword available for use in Call of Duty Online, Call of Duty: Black Ops III, Call of Duty: Infinite Warfare, Call of Duty: Black Ops 4, Call of Duty: Mobile, Call of Duty: Vanguard, Call of Duty: Black Ops 6, and Call of Duty: Black Ops 7. It is also used by the Imperial Japanese Army in Call of Duty: World at War, and makes a brief appearance in Call of Duty: Black Ops, Call of Duty: Black Ops II, Call of Duty: Black Ops Cold War, and Call of Duty: Modern Warfare III.

The Werewolf, known as the WereWOLF in the NES version, is an enemy from the original Final Fantasy. It is a palette swap of the original Wolf, possessing a green back instead of a yellow one. They commonly appear in packs along with Wolves and Warg Wolves. If they attack in a group, the Werewolf can prove troublesome for a weaker team, particularly if they are encountered near Matoya's Cave early in the game. It regenerates three HP each turn and its attacks may inflict the Poison status effect on a party member.

The Weretiger, known as the CATMAN in the Nintendo Entertainment System version, is an enemy from the original Final Fantasy. It appears on the Bahamut Islands, as well as on the first floor of the Mirage Tower. In the Bahamut Islands, they appear flanked by Sabertooth Tigers, while in the Mirage Tower, they appear only with other Weretigers. Weretigers regenerate some HP each turn, but are not hard to beat and the amount of HP they regain does not pose a threat. They also use Poison. When they appear in groups they may be a nuisance, as they resist magic.

The Witch of the Fens is a viera Red Mage who lives in an isolated hut in the Tramdine Fens on the continent of Ordalia in Final Fantasy Tactics A2: Grimoire of the Rift. She plays a key role in a string of quests—the player must bring her the ingredients necessary, and she brews them into the quest item.
Private Kamenetzky is an American soldier who fought in World War II with the 1st Infantry Division under the command of Sgt. Walker, as seen in Call of Duty: Finest Hour.

Wivre is a genus of enemies in Final Fantasy XI. Often raised and trained by the Mamool Ja Savages, Wivre are often used as mounts for the Mamool Ja knight biological class, such as the knight overlord Lancelord Gaheel Ja. Wivre, when not moving, appear to resist frontal and rear attacks. If attacks are made at the front or rear, the damage will be severely reduced. However, if the attacks are done from the sides, the damage appears to be normal. They gain this special "defense" after the use of "Granite Hide", which greatly increases defense to the front and the back, similar to the Quadav move "Diamond Shell", where they become immune to attacks on its shell.
The Yellow Flan is an Lightning-elemental enemy from Final Fantasy XII: Revenant Wings. It is a Rank I Yarhi.

Zalera the Death Seraph, listed as simply Zalera in the in-game bestiary, is an enemy from Final Fantasy Brave Exvius, and exclusively appears in the Final Fantasy Tactics exchange event The Auracite Chosen. He is the boss battle for the stage 'Chosen by the Stone - PRO'.
The OTs-02 Kiparis is a Russian submachine gun featured in Call of Duty: Black Ops, Call of Duty: Black Ops Cold War, and Call of Duty: Mobile.

The Zemzelett is a flying enemy from Final Fantasy IX. The party can find it in the Dead Forest outside the Black Mage Village. It sometimes counters physical attacks with Psychokinesis, so it is best to attack with magic. It is not immune to Silence, which can give an advantage. It is susceptible to Quina's LV4 Holy.

Alebrijes are the colorful, spirit animal inhabitants in the Land of the Dead. Some Alebrijes with owners are the spirit guide of both their owner and their family, just as Pepita is the spirit guide of Imelda Rivera and the Rivera family clan. When they enter the Land of the Living, they take the form of normal animals.

The Brazilian Helicopter Pilot is a character from Inside Out. It is presumed that Riley's mother knew him at some point before marrying Riley's father, and that he had proposed her to stay with him. His memory holds a special place in the mother's mind. When disappointed by her husband, her Anger emotion is shown to mention the pilot frequently, bringing up his memory orb which shows him asking Riley's mother to "come fly with me, gatinha."

The is a melee weapon featured in Call of Duty: Black Ops, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare Remastered, Call of Duty: Mobile and Call of Duty: Modern Warfare III. It is also briefly seen in Call of Duty: Black Ops II, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare, Call of Duty: Vanguard, Call of Duty: Black Ops 6, Call of Duty: Black Ops 7, and Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4.

Evelyn Deavor is a main character in Incredibles 2. She is Winston Deavor's sister and the second-in-command of Devtech. She manipulates a pizza guy, who was given the nickname “Screenslaver”, to do her dirty work and make himself look bad. She is revealed to be the true Screenslaver near the climax of the film, and is subsequently arrested.
The LEGO Bunny is a character in Toy Story OF TERROR!. He is a yellow bunny entirely made out of LEGO bricks. His LEGO nature gives him shape-shifting capacities, enabling him to take various forms.
"Jumping" Jerry Jablonski is a green tentacled monster who works as a Scarer at Monsters, Inc.
Kick is a Weapon Proficiency in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 3. Its icon consists of a bucking horse.

Meilin Lee (born c. 1989) is one of the main characters of the Disney•Pixar film, Turning Red. Mei is a Chinese-Canadian, 13-year-old teenage girl living in Toronto, passing through the trials and tribulations of growing up with the added bonus of turning into a massive red panda every time she feels strong emotions, which, when you’re a teenager, is almost all the time. With her friends, Miriam, Priya, and Abby, they have fun and enjoy a popular boy band called 4*Town. She used to be enemies with Tyler, but after he was revealed as a 4*Townie, Mei became best friends with him. Mei has an overprotective mother, Ming. Ming is not certain about Mei's choices such as her favorite band or her friends.

PR-T is a hair-dessing beautician-bot with a ridiculous amount of arms for beautifying efficiently that is built to serve the Axiom as the one of the grooming type bots, along with HAN-S. She is also one of the minor characters. She also comes with automatic flattery and makes pointless small-talk and usually says "You look gorgeous!" and "Va-va-voom!" as her main catchphrases.

The Kinetic Strike Weapon is an equipment that is used in Call of Duty: Black Ops II campaign.

RC Car is Andy's remote control toy car. He can move on his own, but loses control once someone takes a hold of his remote. He can also communicate only through a series of beeps and whirs, though the toys (specifically Mr. Potato Head) can understand him perfectly.
Skipper Riley is a supporting character in the Cars Toons short Air Mater. He also appears in DisneyToon Studios' Planes and its sequel Planes: Fire & Rescue.

Susan Jensen is a character in Monsters University, and a member of Eta Hiss Hiss. She is a furry purple monster with two green eyes (one of which is unexposed), and purple and maroon hair. She is mentioned in the Monsters University "Official Movie Magazine" published by Disney/Pixar, as having been "raised by circus performers." Therefore, "she's incredibly agile."
The Jungle Warfare Camouflage is a DLC weapon camouflage skin available for Call of Duty: Black Ops II. It is available for anyone who buys the Jungle Warfare Pack for 160 MS Points or $1.99 on PSN.

Baltifer is the name of a cybernetic entity created by , merging the treasonous and the IL-series drone together following the destruction of the life-form known as man. Thus, Baltifer retains many of Baltar's qualities, namely an unbridled thirst for power and an unrelenting desire to utterly subjugate his enemies, perhaps tempered by Lucifer's inclinations of logic. In an alternate reality, Baltifer leads the extermination of humanity's remnants across the galaxy as part of the 's galactic subjugation. This includes preventing the dying doctor Zee from replicating the transformation that created Baltifer for himself. This inspires Zee to continue his efforts at finding other ways to sustain his life, as well as developing technologies for use in Baltifer's (and, to perhaps a lesser extent, the Cylon Empire's) plans ( — ). helps turn the tide against Baltifer's efforts by encouraging the Colonial Resistance, lead by former President , to be more aggressive in their guerrilla warfare. This culminates at a stand-off at the planetoid Cache, where Adama and Apollo present themselves to Baltifer, putting Adama in the position to slay Baltifer and seize command of Baltifer's baseship (—).
The Cylon Centurion is a fully armored, metallic automaton that functions as the basic foot-soldier of the Cylon ground forces.

Dick Durock (18 January 1937—September 2009) was an American stuntman and actor. Starting in 1967, Durock portrayed many characters in many science-fiction and drama TV shows of the 1960s through the mid-1990s. Quoting Durock from his biographical notes from his official web site: :"You'll notice in the Filmography that in my career I've had a pretty liberal sprinkling of shows in the Sci-fi genre. Mainly, however, I usually played big mean thugs who the hero of whatever show I was doing at the time and would beat the %$@&^# out of. From Clint Eastwood and Charlie Bronson, etc., in feature films to Jim Garner, Tom Selleck, Lee Majors and whole bunch of others in TV. I worked a lot because of my size (6'5"- 215lbs) and kind of a rough look. Film heroes like to beat up guys bigger than they are....makes them look good and believe me, I made a lot of them look good over the years." Durock had supporting or minor roles in classic SF such as Star Trek, The Incredible Hulk and Buck Rogers in the 25th Century. Durock gained his own stardom as the lead in the movie, Swamp Thing, co-starring with actress Adrienne Barbeau. Durock portrayed the uncredited role of the Imperious Leader in the episode "Saga of a Star World."
The K7 is a submachine gun that appears in Call of Duty: Ghosts. Like the Honey Badger and the VKS, it has an integrated Silencer.

Lord Erebus is an Imperious Leader for the Cylon Empire. Erebus leads the Cylon task force known as Cylon Fleet Gamma against the Twelve Colonies during the beginning of the Cylon War, and was especially interested in Lt. William Adama, whom it was believed would one day lead the Colonials (and thus, the Cylons) to the lost tribe of Colonists. Little is known about the being that called itself Erebus beyond speculation and ill-remembered myths. A dark, devious and hate-filled individual, Erebus was driven by a desire to wipe out all humans, a species he saw as inferior. Not a native of the Cylon Alliance, he apparently only served the Cylons only because it furthered his own ends. Some observers believed that Erebus was an incredibly long-lived being, possibly one of the mythic Lords of Kobol who were the progenitors of the Colonial peoples. Ancient records from the Tombs of speak of Erebus being exiled from his race for terrible crimes, and of his metahuman abilities that allow him to predict future events and project telekinetic force with his mind. Although it cannot be confirmed, it was suspected that Erebus commanded the Cylon forces that attacked Sagitara early in the war; it was during this assault that William Adama’s father was killed and Bryn Magus was captured and imprisoned. All that Commander Adama finds of his wife in the bombed-out remains of his Caprican home is a picture of her, along with pictures of their children .
